# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

No respondent carries the name of a commenter, customer or founder.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

insights.line: What made the others more pressing?

whys.g1: Both answers say the schedule and getting subs on site beat the daily log, so one group named Keeping the schedule on track is exactly how a super would sort them.
whys.g2: There is no junk, explicit or off-topic answer on this line, so nothing junk was grouped.

founder.order_why: The flow runs sensibly from naming to context to problem to sending, but the context screen comes back at 5 after the look-back question at 4, so the window question sits oddly in the middle of one context step.
founder.asked_twice: Screens 3 and 5 (same kicker and the same question, 'Before we test anything, let's define exactly where this idea applies.')
founder.missing: Nothing asks how long the log takes them (my whole case is 'up to 3 hours a day' in the trailer), and nothing asks who pays: the general contractor buys per site, not the superintendent. The solution (narrated videos turned into notes and pushed to Procore/ACC) and the $1k-per-site-per-month price are never asked either, unless this run is meant to test the problem only.

PRIMARY.order_why: Asking which thing I'd most like made easier comes before asking how my last daily log actually went, so I'm picking a wish before I've walked back through the real day.
PRIMARY.asked_twice: Screens 2 and 3 overlap a little: whether I typed up notes in the last 5 days, then on how many days. It reads as a lead-in, not a true repeat.
PRIMARY.missing: How long the log took me that day, and the photo side of it: getting the day's photos uploaded and tagged in Procore, which eats more of my time than typing the notes. Also whether the log ever got used later, like in a delay dispute with the owner.

screens.why2: Each option says plainly what the super will see and do (a video voice, read and tap, or their choice), so I get it on first read.
screens.why3: I know my supers: they're in the trailer or on the truck with a phone, and I can judge whether they'd rather tap through or talk to a video.
screens.why4: The three options are distinct and cover the real choice (voice, text, or both), and none is missing or silly.
screens.why5: Nothing of Fresco or my roles is bent here; it only asks about the study's format and keeps my 'construction superintendents' wording.

screens.why1: After choosing who interviews and how, picking who gets the link is the obvious last step before sending.
screens.why2: Mostly plain, but 'the Contacts page' and 'signs in with Google' are Keel's own terms that I'd need to read twice to place, and the second option's description runs long.
screens.why3: I know exactly who I'd send to: the supers we met driving to Napa and the South Bay, and the GCs we asked for introductions to.
screens.why4: Named people, a Keel-found list and an open group link cover the ways I'd reach supers, they are distinct, and I picked the first without hesitation.
screens.why5: Nothing of my product is changed or exposed; the screen only asks how the links go out.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' is stated with 'Frequency: 4 counted' beside it, but the line doesn't give the 5 needed, and it names only Frequency when Importance and Current solution are short by the same margin, so I have to read the cards to see why.
screens.why_b2: The tally (1 holding, 3 too few, 7 answered) and each card's bar read plainly, but the kicker's '4 TO 7 COUNTED' takes a second look before I see that 3 of my 7 superintendents weren't counted on three cards, and nothing says why.
screens.why_b3: Importance and Current solution carry the exact belief lines I checked on the way in, and the dimension names are the ones I saw.
screens.why_b4: '5 needed to call it' hints that I need one more counted answer, but the page never says to get more superintendents through, or what the one holding belief, Prevalence, means for Fresco.
screens.why_b5: n=7 stays visible, the low counts are called 'too few to call', and Prevalence at 6 of 7 is called 'at the bar', not strong; my own pitch sits under the verdict, but it reads as my statement, not a finding.
screens.instead: Too few to call: Frequency, Importance and Current solution each counted 4 of 7 superintendents and need 5, so get at least one more answer that counts; only Prevalence holds, at the bar (6 of 7).

screens.why_b1: "Holding up" sits right beside "6 of 7 said yes · bar 6 of 7 · at the bar", so I know it held and that it held by exactly the bar.
screens.why_b2: The strip shows 6 for and 1 against out of 7 on a 0-to-7 axis, with my bar marked at 6 and labelled "at least 8 in 10", so the count, the base and the bar are plain at once.
screens.why_b3: My problem was typing up the daily log, but the card and the gate say "typed up site notes after their walks", which is close to what every super does anyway; it's recognisable but softer than my belief, and "the most recent time it happened" doesn't fit a yes/no gate.
screens.why_b4: "How often, and whether it matters, are the next two cards" points me onward, but it doesn't say what clearing the bar with one person to spare means for Fresco.
screens.why_b5: n=7 stays visible, the one No is shown and counted, and "a small group: a lean, not a call" plus "at your bar exactly" keep it from being called strong.
screens.instead: Holding up, just: 6 of 7 supers typed up the daily log after their walks this week, exactly your bar of 8 in 10, so one more No would flip it; with only 7 people this is a lean. Check Frequency and Importance before treating the log as the pain to sell on.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right beside its deciding number, '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', and the So line repeats both, so I know exactly why there's no call yet.
screens.why_b2: Working days out of 5 and the bar at 4 of 5 are clear, but the legend's 'what you said' and 'at what you said' look like the same thing, the axis starts at 0 though nobody could answer 0, and I have to count strip cells to see how many people the chart is over.
screens.why_b3: 4 to 5 working days out of 5 is my number, but 'type up site notes after their walks' is not quite how I'd say it; in my trade it's the daily log, which is what I typed in.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is true but generic; it doesn't tell me that one more counted superintendent would settle it, or that all four so far are in my range.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible (6 answered, 4 counted, why Hank and Luis are out), the small group is called 'a lean, not a call', and the screen doesn't claim a hold from four people, though the trailing 'the most recent time it happened' after the question is stray wording rather than an overstatement.
screens.instead: Too few to call: all 4 superintendents counted logged it on 4 or 5 of the last 5 working days. One more counted answer decides it, so send the study to one more superintendent.

screens.why_b1: The verdict, Too few to call, sits right beside the number that decides it: 4 counted, 5 needed to call it.
screens.why_b2: The bars plainly count 8 picks from 4 people, and my item's 2 against 3 and 3 for schedule and subs is clear, but the strip's 'your bar · 4 of 5' takes a second look before I see it means 4 of 5 must put it in their two, not 4 counted out of 5.
screens.why_b3: The card is named Importance and the belief line is word for word the one I checked, with 'Typing up the day's daily log' as my item.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic: it doesn't say I need one more superintendent counted, or that at 2 for and 2 against, schedule and subs are already outdrawing the log.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible (6 answered, 4 counted, with why Hank and Luis aren't counted), the small group is called out, and nothing claims more than a 2-2 split can carry.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 2 of 4 put the daily log in their two, and schedule and subs drew more picks (3 each); get one more superintendent counted, and if they also pass it over, the log isn't their top pain.

screens.why_b1: The status *Too few to call* sits right beside *4 counted · 5 needed to call it*, and the So line says the same, so I know where I stand and why.
screens.why_b2: The rungs, the line and the per-rung counts read at once, but the strip's *your bar · 4 of 5* with its marker at 4 and a ghost cell took me a second look: I couldn't tell at first whether 4 of 5 was my score or the bar on five people, while only 3 count for me.
screens.why_b3: The title is Current solution, the belief is word for word the one I checked, and the bar names my rung *Done in the trailer in under an hour*.
screens.why_b4: *Nothing is settled here yet* is generic: it doesn't say that 3 of the 4 counted fell short (a lean my way) or that one more counted superintendent would settle it.
screens.why_b5: n is on the screen (6 answered, 4 counted, who was dropped and why), the small group is called a lean and not a call, and nothing is claimed beyond those people.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 3 of the 4 counted fell short of 'Done in the trailer in under an hour', a lean your way; one more counted superintendent decides it.

screens.why_b1: The box opens on 'Too few to call' with '4 counted · 5 needed to call it' right beside it, so I know there's no verdict yet and exactly why.
screens.why_b3: It says Importance and my belief word for word, the five hard things after the walks and the daily log as one of the two I'd most like made easier.
screens.why_b4: '5 needed' tells me to get one more answer, but nothing says what two of four putting the schedule and subs above the log means for a scribe sold on saving the super's evening.
screens.why_b5: Every count is small and shown (2 against, 2 asked, 4 counted), the line is plainly marked too few to call, and nothing is claimed beyond the people who answered.
screens.why_b6: I didn't type this: what beats the log is subs not showing and the schedule slipping, and 'the log can wait till morning, the deck can't' tells me the log isn't urgent, even for a super who does it on the tablet before leaving the gate.
screens.instead: Two of the four counted put keeping the schedule and getting subs to show up above the log, which they say can wait till morning; one more answer calls it. The Current solution line has no box here and should say why.

screens.why1: As the first screen it checks whether my jobs are on the software the study is about, which makes sense before anything else.
screens.why2: Procore and ACC are what every super I know works in, so I can answer at once, even if 'running now run on' doubles up a bit.
screens.why3: I know exactly which platform each of my jobs is on.
screens.why4: Yes or No covers it, and a screener needs no escape.
screens.why5: It names the platforms the founder's segment is about and nothing of the product itself.
screens.why6: It is short and one question, ACC is said as letters on site anyway, and 'Yes; or No' is easy to hold.
screens.instead: Are any of your current jobs on Procore or ACC? Yes; or No.

screens.why1: Right after asking if my jobs run on Procore or ACC, asking whether I typed things up after my walks this week is the obvious next step.
screens.why2: Typing up notes after a walk is plain to me on one hearing, though I'd call what I type up the daily log.
screens.why3: I know exactly whether I sat in the trailer this week and typed up what I saw on the walks.
screens.why4: Yes and No cover it, and the chips belong to the story box after a Yes, not to this question.
screens.why5: The founder's problem is typing up the daily log after the walks, and *site notes* drifts a little from that, while the next screen jumps back to *your last daily log*.
screens.why6: One short question and then *Yes or no*, easy to answer once heard.
screens.why7: Two fixed answers with no escape, and the stem asks the after-the-walk typing rather than the walk itself, so a super who logs on the walk can truly say No and one who types it up later says Yes.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, did you type up the daily log after your site walks? Yes or no.

screens.why1: Right after I said yes to typing up notes after my walks, asking on how many of those five days it happened is the obvious next question.
screens.why2: Plain to me: five working days, site notes, walks are how I'd say it, though I'd more likely call it doing the daily log.
screens.why3: I know which days this week I sat down after walking the job and put my notes in, so I can count it without guessing.
screens.why4: One button per working day from 1 to 5 covers every true answer, none overlap, and I can't recall fits as the one way out.
screens.why5: It asks about my own end-of-walk paperwork and nothing of anybody's product, plan or labels for me comes through.
screens.why6: One short question, then a number from 1 to 5 and can't recall, which I can hear once and answer in a word.
screens.why7: Every option counts working days on the one measure, the unit is said and then said again short, the buttons run 1 to 5 with no 0 and no bands, I can't recall is the only escape, and nothing on this screen stops the founder's low from splitting the buttons.

screens.why1: Right after asking how many days I typed up notes after my walks, it makes sense to ask which part of my day I'd most like made easier.
screens.why2: Subs, RFIs, submittals and the daily log are all words I use every day on a Procore job, so I can answer it on first read or first hearing.
screens.why3: Every one of these is something I deal with myself on my own site, so I can answer from my last day without guessing.
screens.why4: Getting subs to show up and finish is most of what keeping the job on schedule means to me, so those two overlap, and RFIs and submittals are two different chases jammed into one option.
screens.why5: Nothing of the product leaks to me, but the founder's problem was getting the photos and the notes into the daily log, and the photos dropped out of the row, even though uploading them is the hours-long part.
screens.why6: It's one short question with five short options I can hold in my head, and the escape is said last.
screens.why7: The own item is there and not first, and the belief can go either way, but the other rows are whole-job headaches rather than what's hard once the walks are done, one is a cause of another (subs, then schedule), and one row holds two things.
screens.instead: Think of your last day on site. Which one of these would you most like made easier? Getting the day's photos and notes into the daily log · Writing up the walk's punch items · Sending the subs their open items · Answering RFIs at the end of the day · None of these

screens.why1: After asking which part of my last day I'd most like made easier, asking how my last daily log actually went is the obvious next step.
screens.why2: Daily log is my word, but 'typing up the daily log from the photos in the trailer' stacks the tool, the place and the act into one stem I'd have to read twice.
screens.why3: I write the daily log myself every day, so I know exactly how the last one went.
screens.why4: 'Log done on site' doesn't answer a question that already put me in the trailer, and 'took a couple of hours after the walk' and 'finished at home or the next morning' can both be true of the same night.
screens.why5: Nothing about the product or the founder's plan reaches me; trailer, photos and daily log are my own world.
screens.why6: The five options say well as a list, but the stem's 'typing up the daily log from the photos in the trailer' is a mouthful to hear once.
screens.why7: The shape holds, with two working rungs above a line, three shortfalls below and the last rung never getting done, but the rungs mix where and when the log got finished with how long it took, which bends the one measure of time the card asks for.
screens.instead: Think of your last daily log. How long did writing it up take? Under 30 minutes; 30 minutes to an hour; one to two hours; over two hours; or it never got written up properly. Or say someone else wrote it.
